title: Hollandaise Sauce
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, made by emulsifying egg yolks with warm clarified butter and brightened with lemon juice, creating a rich, velvety sauce for eggs, fish, and vegetables.

items: 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice (or white wine vinegar reduction)
A pinch of cayenne pepper or white pepper

instructions: Fill a saucepan with a small amount of water and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Place the egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof stainless-steel bowl over the bain-marie, ensuring the bowl does not touch the water.
Whisk continuously until the mixture becomes pale, thick, and forms ribbons.
Remove the bowl from direct heat and slowly drizzle in the warm clarified butter while whisking constantly to create a smooth emulsion.
Continue whisking until the sauce is thick, glossy, and silky.
Season with salt, cayenne pepper or white pepper, and adjust the acidity with additional lemon juice if desired.
Serve immediately or keep warm over lukewarm water, avoiding excessive heat to prevent the sauce from splitting.
chefTips: Maintain gentle heat throughout the process to avoid scrambling the egg yolks.
Add the clarified butter slowly to achieve a stable emulsion.
If the sauce becomes too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water.
Hollandaise is the base for Béarnaise, Mousseline, and Maltaise sauces.
Best served with Eggs Benedict, steamed fish, asparagus, and other delicate vegetables.
